docs.title: Logical Architecture
docs.text: Layers: Client, Edge, Core. See blueprint Part III for detail.

docs.title: Irreducible Trade-offs
docs.text:
Choice Gain Loss On-device AI Privacy, offline latency Model quality, update velocity, device cost Federated learning Privacy, scale Convergence speed, debugging difficulty BT mesh Offline safety Battery, complexity, security surface OSM base layer Cost, openness Freshness, completeness Community data Coverage, cost Trust, validation load Cross-platform Reach Performance parity, native feature access Temporal layers Rich context Storage explosion, query complexity

Key Decision: Privacy over model quality; offline over fresh. Correct strategic bet, requires architectural compensation.

docs.title: Six Irreducible Mandates
docs.text: ID Objective Architectural Mandate Success Metric O1 AI-powered smart shortcuts Real-time graph optimization with multi-objective cost functions Route quality > Google/Waze in blind A/B tests O2 Privacy-first design Zero-knowledge architecture; no PII at rest or in transit Zero data-breach blast radius O3 Cross-platform delivery Single logical system, multiple render targets Feature parity within 2 weeks of release O4 Offline-full AI On-device inference parity with cloud <5% quality delta offline vs online O5 Community-powered data Byzantine-fault-tolerant contribution pipeline >95% report accuracy at scale O6 Bluetooth mesh safety Sub-100ms peer-to-peer hazard propagation 30% accident reduction in pilot zones

docs.title: Tension Web
docs.text:
Mandates are not independent:

  • O2 (privacy) constrains O5 (community data)
  • O4 (offline) limits AI model size, constraining O1 (shortcut quality)
  • O6 (mesh latency) forces edge-first processing with zero cloud dependency

This tension is the central architectural challenge.
